goals.1: The modal verb in second place, the main verb at the end
goals.2: Talking about languages: Ich spreche ein bisschen Deutsch
dialog.1.de.3.n: Language names are capitalised and have no article: Bengalisch, Englisch, Deutsch
dialog.2.de.0.n: du kannst — the modal verb is in second place
dialog.2.de.5.n: The main verb goes at the end, in the infinitive (sprechen)
dialog.3.de.5.n: ich kann — ich and er have the same form
dialog.5.de.1.n: ich will = I want (a firm wish); more politely: ich möchte
dialog.6.de.1.n: du musst — müssen = to have to
grammar.0.title: Full table of modal verbs
grammar.0.note: ich and er/sie/es have the same form (no -e or -t) — the biggest feature of modal verbs.
grammar.1.title: The modal in second place, the main verb at the end
grammar.1.text: The modal verb goes in second place, and the main verb goes to the end of the sentence in the infinitive (-en) — like Bangla “… korte pari”.
grammar.2.intro: sprechen: e → i with du and er.
grammar.2.note: To say which language you speak: Ich spreche Deutsch. (no article).
quiz.3.why: ich kann (ich and er have the same form).
quiz.6.sub: I want to work in Germany.
quiz.6.why: The modal is in second place; the main verb is at the end in the infinitive.
